This app plans your gym sessions, guides every set and adjusts to how you feel. Everything stays on your phone: no account, no internet.
It is not a medical device and does not diagnose or treat anything. If you have a health condition, check with your doctor before starting a new exercise plan.
Setup takes about 5 minutes. You can change your answers later.
These decide how carefully the first weeks start. Please answer each one.
Has a doctor said you have a heart condition, or high blood pressure that isn’t controlled?
Do you have diabetes, kidney disease or lung disease?
In the past 12 months, have you had chest pain, fainting, unexplained dizziness, or unusual breathlessness at rest or with light effort?
Do you have palpitations or a known heart-rhythm problem?
Has a doctor told you to limit exercise for any reason, or are you pregnant or recently postpartum?
Do you have a bone, joint or soft-tissue problem that exercise could worsen?
Do you take medicine for a long-term condition such as blood pressure or heart disease?
For the last 3 months, have you exercised on purpose at least 3 days a week for 30+ minutes at moderate effort?
Thanks. You can start with the standard plan.
Thanks. You’ll train at moderate effort for now. Please check with your doctor before hard or interval training; once they agree, you can say so in Settings.
Please check with your doctor before starting. Until you confirm they are happy for you to exercise, the plan stays gentle: no hard intervals, and every set stops well before failure.
Follow your doctor’s or midwife’s guidance first. The plan stays gentle.
You mentioned a joint problem or a long-term medicine: if you are unsure about an exercise, check with your clinician.

If you feel ill, tell today\'s check-in: it asks about illness and makes the day lighter or a rest day. If you have a fever or it gets worse, see a doctor.
If something hurts during a workout, tap Something hurts: the app stops or changes that exercise. Before training, tell the check-in. If pain lasts, see a physiotherapist or a doctor.
